correctness.rationale: The off-center-section lemma proves that an r-cube hyperplane section with all \(r\ge3\) positive coefficients, nonzero t, and \(|t|\) below the coefficient sum is centrally symmetric only when one coefficient dominates the sum of the others plus |t|. Its proof tracks unique restricted coordinate facet directions, opposite facet pairing, and boundedness; both implications include equality. Applied to the largest-coordinate face of a nondominant central slice, it produces an exposed face with no center; zonoid exposed faces always have centers. Dominant and \(m\le3\)-support cases are explicit cube or centrally symmetric planar products. Exact rational test code checks 289 normal quadruples, six 5-coordinate cases, 896 off-center 3-cube sections, and five dominant cases; these tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The theorem answers the specific sharp necessity question left open by a full primary paper: which centered cube hyperplane slices retain zonoid structure. It is an all-dimension natural complete classification with a sharp coefficient boundary, covers nongeneric degeneracies and yields an explicit noncentrally symmetric exposed-face certificate outside the domain. This is more than a named substitution, bounded calculation or textbook equivalence.
